reviews.text: Fans of the John Wick series and anyone stuck in a career rut will enjoy this ludicrously plotted revenge.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Nobody ... makes no false pretenses in its practical re-creation of the Wick franchise
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: You will not believe how smooth and just flat-out joyous a movie like this is with Odenkirk doling out the punishment. It’s just a delight.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It has a fast-paced start that often benefits from Bob Odenkirk's physical prowess for action sequences, but unfortunately it often stumbles over a regular tone that prevents it from escaping the clichés of the genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: ... A film that aims nothing more than to play with genre boundaries to put the action story back into work; well-told, better-filmed, and one hundred percent delightful. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Odenkirk submits his action hero punch card & can take my money any day of the week with it all. It knows how wild it is & it goes about it in spades with its 90 minute runtime
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Despite its intentions, Nobody feels condescending and portentous far more often than it actually feels campy and self-aware.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: …Nobody’s standard-issue plotting and tired male posturing land far short of the B-Movie classic it aspires to, but there is enough brisk action and some bonuses, largely through the casting of veterans like Michael Ironside and Christopher Lloyd…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Nobody is a bone-crunching, knuckle-busting, lip-splitting action film that has every intention of dragging you across concrete with the taste of asphalt in your mouth and bits of glass in your forehead.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Nobody is an arresting action showcase for star Bob Odenkirk and a skillfully staged spectacle of stuntwork nearly on par with the John Wick trilogy.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: A unique take on the action genre, Nobody is lean, mean, and showcases a delightful Odenkirk leading the way through all the carnage.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: As “Nobody” propels forward the violence gets crazier and the body count mounts. Yet the movie never loses its self-awareness.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Nobody feels like the cinematic brother to one of my favourite films of recent years, Michael Caine's Harry Brown, equally as violent and satisfying.
reviews.author: Cris Kennedy

reviews.text: A well-executed and fun film full of gunfire left and right... There's never a surplus of those. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Hardly an enlightened examination of modern manhood.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: In a world filled with a recent collection of well-made action films, Nobody is a great addition to this action renaissance. If this is the Bob Odenkirk John Wick, when can we expect the Rhea Seehorn Atomic Blonde?
reviews.author: Amanda Mazzillo

reviews.text: Nobody will thrill people who fancy some violent laughs. Its perhaps best summed up by Lloyds assessment of his sons handiwork  excessive, but glorious!
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: The director's knack for bravado action shines in part because Kolstad's script makes us care about Hutch, but we only care because he is perfectly cast.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: In a world full of tough talkers who boast what theyd do if given half a chance, heres a refreshing reminder what you dont know is reason enough to probably leave someone alone.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Even better is Odenkirk who trained for two years to become an action hero - and owns it.
reviews.author: Alex Behan

reviews.text: Odenkirk is unsurprisingly brilliant, and the film is a hell of a lot of fun.
reviews.author: George Fenwick

reviews.text: In all honesty the most creative part of Nobody is how Kolstad has effectively sold the same screenplay twice to two different movie studios.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: The fight sequences and stunt choreography are first class, as is the slyly calibrated performance of Odenkirk as Hutch.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Bloody, crowd-pleasing, brutal, and fun, Nobody is a surprisingly great action movie.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: Odenkirk is a delight, as he is in everything he does.
reviews.author: Jason Shawhan

reviews.text: The genius to put Bob Odenkirk, Christopher LLoyd and the RZA on a battlefield together? It cannot be ignored.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: It kinda makes me chuckle at how Nobody is really a movie about how pulverizing being a responsible adult can be.
reviews.author: Craig D. Lindsey

reviews.text: Although Nobody has its fair share of inventive action sequences, it really lives and dies on the strength of Odenkirk's performance and his charismatic screen presence.
reviews.author: Audrey Fox

reviews.text: John Wick has been there and done it better.
reviews.author: Scroll Staff

reviews.text: Nobody is equal parts Keanu Reeves John Wick and Bill Hader's Barry with a touch of escape from suburbia... and 100% Action fest. That being said, please Hollywood people don't turn Bob Odenkirk into the next Liam Neeson.
reviews.author: Alejandro Turdó

reviews.text: It's the movie Liam Neeson would have made if Bob Odenkirk hadn't make it. (Universal blu-ray).
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Naishuller also understands these kinds of heavy action films need lighter moments. The family scenes come across as a little stilted but there are moments when Hutch is allowed to dip into some dark humor that really works.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: There's nothing particularly new here, but the film does seem aware of that fact and has a huge amount of fun with its basic premise.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Just really entertaining, A-list B-movie exploitation trash done really well. I watched the whole film with a grin on my face.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: File this one alongside last year's Unhinged as a guilty pleasure you really shouldn't feel guilty about for one second.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: "Nobody" is short and sweet. There's lots of value in it's simplicity. Odenkirk's performance alone is enough to make this film worth watching.
reviews.author: Susan Kamyab

reviews.text: Unapologetic, intentionally disruptive and grounded by a persuasive performance, Nobody demonstrates that Liam Neeson is no longer cornering the market when it comes to action star reinvention.
reviews.author: Martin Carr

reviews.text: Ok, this isn't Citizen Kane, but it does exactly what it sets out to do without any hesitation or deviation, though perhaps some repetition.
reviews.author: Adam Sweeting

reviews.text: Odenkirk is the true reason to see this film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: It's 90 minutes of super fast, fun entertainment with a balanced mix of action and dark humor. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alejandro G. Calvo

reviews.text: This could have been so provocative.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk doesn't miss a beat in Ilya Naishuller fun, dumb and thoroughly daft vigilante thriller.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: Featuring viscerally violent set pieces and a surprisingly impressive action lead in Bob Odenkirk, Nobody is an absurdly fun thriller
reviews.author: Nicola Austin

reviews.text: It's a blast.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Odenkirk, so wonderful as a seedy lawyer in the TV drama Breaking Bad and its spin-off Better Call Saul, proves unexpectedly convincing as an action hero. And it's always a pleasure to see Christopher Lloyd, who pops up as his old dad.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: White collar John Wick, Nobody has plenty of blistering instances of violence and carnage, but lacks those flourishes that made its peer so successful.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: A kicky, flashy action thriller...
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: Thankfully, Odenkirk remains wry and watchable... It's just enough to make you wish he might cross paths with Mr Wick in the future.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Nobody never relies on the greatness of the cast or the safety of the premise. Instead, it stands on its feet as an instant thrill-inducing classic that is sure to charm audiences all around.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: The fun is only somewhat diminished by a muddled commentary on toxic masculinity. Nonetheless, Odenkirk's ferocious performance quickly pulls viewers back into the action for an experience audiences won't soon forget.
reviews.author: Andrew Murray

reviews.text: Derek Kolstad... gives Odenkirk enough room to slyly acknowledge the regressive nature of this film's plot while simultaneously embracing the opportunity to have fun going kill-crazy on a bunch of Russian mobsters.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The movie gets blood on the carpet with grim pizzazz but a striking lack of humour.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: As far as action stardom goes, Odenkirk might yet be somebody.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: With Better Call Saul about to come to an end, Odenkirk switches gears with admirable ease, anchoring one of the most purely enjoyable action movies in ages. It's not quite a case of Nobody does it better, but it'll do until somebody does.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt (UK)

reviews.text: It's a slick and peppily-helmed operation and fans of hyper-stylised carnage will get more than their money's worth.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: The cast of Nobody transcends the material. I liked this journey and I liked this character.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Great fun but don't expect much originality.
reviews.author: Lou Thomas

reviews.text: What if Bob Odenkirk was John Wick?
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: Odenkirk shines in this absurdly funny, visually stylish and extremely bloody revenge thriller. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: However, Nobody oozes with irony and a sense of its own absurdity, delivered with deadpan aplomb by Odenkirk...
reviews.author: Jeremy Aspinall

reviews.text: Seriously...is there anything Bob Odenkirk is NOT great at?
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: This film is just angry, a deadening thud of pointless nihilism that actually seems to celebrate saving a marriage through mass murder.
reviews.author: Stephen A. Russell

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk is a new action hero with whom it is easy to relate. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: Ilya Naishuller's directing is spot on and imaginative. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emmanuel Báez

reviews.text: The best successor to John Wick that Hollywood has given us so far. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: An hour and a half that portrays acidly the midlife crisis in some sort of 'American Beauty' loaded to the brim with blood, gunpowder, piles of dead bodies and a charm just comparable to the overwhelming charisma of its main star.
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: Mostly, [Odenkirk is] just an enormously talented actor who instinctively makes risky choices and pulls them off.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: Naishuller and Odenkirk are on to something with the title character, an anonymous dad with deadly hands. It will not be surprising to see him do his taxes, mow the lawn and wipe out an army of thugs - in that order.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: A violent movie about the routine as a safe place and how this one lack in our everyday life. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: Nobody is nothing major, but there's enough funny and electrifying moments laced through the uneven plot sequences to make us engaged.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk shines in this bloody actioner.
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: [There is a] constant, frenetic and well-crafted amount of shocking action that the public expects, although the story lacks emotional impact. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Fernando Galván

reviews.text: You can't be serious. This is an empty kind of nasty, and in the end, who stands to benefit? The answer is right there in the title.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: [Ilya] Naishuller knows well enough how to stage a brutal action scene that feels both visceral, gritty and thrilling.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: I found myself marveling at the fight choreography and cackling at unexpected developments. Nobody offers a lot of wit to go with its gore.
reviews.author: Scott Phillips

reviews.text: Nobody is more a celebratory wallow than a warning.
reviews.author: Walter Chaw

reviews.text: A suit made to measure for the actor who doesn't pretend to be the new Liam Neeson. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Irene Crespo

reviews.text: Odenkirk proves he has the goods as he shifts from character actor to leading man.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: Hutch ain't no Saul, but he is an entertaining distraction...
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Is it realistic? Gedoudda here. It's a cartoon. But as directed by Ilya Naishuller and written by Derek Kolstad, it's made by people who know what they're doing.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: The brilliant casting of unassuming comedian Bob Odenkirk... makes his character Hutch Mansell believable.
reviews.author: Jonathan Roberts

reviews.text: Thanks to Odenkirk, Nobody gets to rise above the bare-bones way it answers its what-ifs.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: An amusing but forgettable action comedy that never escapes the shadow of "John Wick." [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: I don't really know why I didn't hate Nobody, but the fact that I didn't must mean something.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: It's a notch below the John Wick franchise but it's still a fun, entertaining feature.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: A stellar piece of hard-boiled pulp.
reviews.author: Allen Almachar

reviews.text: I'm not sure anyone but Odenkirk could have pulled off this thematic bait-and-switch so well, but the end result is a film that lays bare the calculus of movie violence.
reviews.author: Ben Kuchera

reviews.text: In short: a lot of balls and fury signifying...not much.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: ...boasts a surprisingly engrossing (and believable) tough-guy turn by Odenkirk.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: [Bob Odenkirk is] a great actor, and he gets to show that in here because.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Yes, this is basically a rewrite of the first John Wick, but Odenkirk finds an entirely different way into it - expanding on Hutch's shadowy backstory with a nuanced performance that sets him completely apart...
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: This is not an emotionally deep film, but it does raise interesting questions about whether the life we once lived is the one we prefer.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: Like Liam Neeson who was Taken before him, Bob Odenkirk has surprisingly joined the list of violent cinema daddies who would rather catch a body than buy a boat to assuage their quiet discontentment with life.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Nobody is wild, OTT fun that might not work without Odenkirk's full-bore performance.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Great story, pacing and soundtrack and Odenkirk is phenomenal.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Nobody is more than its stunt casting, but its intentionally unremarkable title ends up being all too accurate for this run-of-the-mill (if well-crafted) shoot-em-up.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: It's a different kind of project for Odenkirk, and it's also a wonderful re-invention of the actor himself who might just have entered in to yet another iconic role.
reviews.author: Felix Vasquez Jr.

reviews.text: With a nod toward film noir - there's an out-of-focus poster for Orson Welles' Touch of Evil (1953) in the family basement - Naishuller offers a darker side to fatherhood than the first few minutes of the film suggest.
reviews.author: Elias Savada

reviews.text: Nobody is as visceral and smashing as it ludicrous and bonkers, and it is every bit the flashy and vigorously violent movie you'd expect to match its enormously high body count.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: This genre film is quite violent and unbelievable, but it is so witty, so unserious and so well crafted that it is fun to watch.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: Naishuller keeps the pace cooking with inventive showdowns and gallows humor, all filmed like he's got one shot to prove his worth.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: The film is really kind of ridiculous, and it knows it. That's what makes it fun.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: Pure fun, pure adrenaline.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: All about the ever-watchable Odenkirk and his peerless and compelling ability to play slippery characters.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk? This is like finding out that Parker Posey really wishes she were Pamela Anderson-a deflating insight.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: Nobody is an action packed free-for-all chock-full of gloriously exhausting bone crunching and skin tearing spectacles. Bob Odenkirk is the obscenity-spewing, balls of steel action star we never knew we needed.
reviews.author: Chris Sawin

reviews.text: The near super-human powers of the protagonist become difficult to accept, but you're still rooting for him and this skillfully made movie... strong enough to inspire likely sequels.
reviews.author: Michael Medved

reviews.text: Christopher Lloyd, 82, is having a moment. After playing wingman to William Shatner's late-life Romeo in Senior Moment, the Back to the Future star gets the film's biggest laughs as Mansell's Pops.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: Lil' Bobby Odenkirk...MY HERO!!!
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: While Nobody can be taken as a species of parody, Odenkirk never lets on. The ability to deliver lines like "Give me the kitty-cat bracelet" with total, grim conviction: that too could be seen as heroism, of a sort.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: To steal a quote from "Robocop (1987)," "I like it!"
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: Nobody is an absolute blast from start to finish. It delivers all the snarky comedy/bloody action one would want and brings a new and amazing action hero into the midst with Bob Odenkirk who is amazing as Hutch. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Made for box-office success and to give the undemanding viewers all the familiar thrills they never seem to tire of.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: ...if you're in the mood for an utterly engaging character study, with a beautifully realised performance from Odenkirk and truly spectacular kicky-punchy action then, well, Nobody's perfect.
reviews.author: Anthony O'Connor

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk makes this film-which has a great soundtrack-sing loud and clear for 91 minutes. He's a more relatable and funny man with a particular set of skills.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: There are good reasons to watch Nobody. Whatever you do, however, don't think about it.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: The impressively hard-hitting violence is too good to dismiss the film entirely, but the script is too dodgy to feel like it's an easy recommendation.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: You know what? It doesn't matter how much cinema changes or how woke it becomes, the appeal of cathartic, righteously motivated movie violence will never fade. That's the hard, not-altogether-surprising truth at the heart of this old-style vigilante romp.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: There is nothing new or fresh about "Nobody," it just sticks there like a retread of better and more invigorating movies.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: At first seems like a Death Wish or Liam Neeson ripoff, but in the end it's a really impressive and enjoyable action movie
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: A festival of violence...it sounds and feels so familiar.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Even in a movie with a fundamentally retrograde worldview, you want to root for this goofy guy.
reviews.author: Dan Jackson

reviews.text: Nobody peaked at around the 30-minute mark, and everything that came after was disappointingly daft, lazily implausible and tiresomely derivative.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: What makes this fantasy of cowboy-style self-defense so disturbing is that it isn't limited to the movies. It's the very same belief system that gets used, in real life, to justify the American obsession with gun ownership.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: You almost expect to see Wile E. Coyote leaping off a cliff with an Acme anvil on his back.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: Kolstad's script hits on family values, revenge elements, domestic espionage and financial improprieties. The dialogue is juicy.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: It was really, really fun. I loved the whole family element of it.
reviews.author: Achara Kirk

reviews.text: Short and to the point and it did a really really good job at that.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: Odenkirk sells it with wicked pleasure, making it worthwhile to follow him through every punch, kick, dive and shootout.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: Better Call Saul fans will love seeing this side of Odenkirk, and Nobody is wonderful because of, not in spite of, its lead actor. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Father's day came early this year!
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: "Nobody" earns its keep.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: a wildly entertaining ride that's unapologetically outrageous, campy and wickedly funny.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: "Nobody" makes me want to see somebody such as Bob Odenkirk in future action thrillers - perhaps as the same character.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: "Nobody" is a wild ride that goes a bit too far but is bolstered by terrific stunt work.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk - who can take way more punches than he gives - and the impressively brutal fight scenes raise this above a story that goes beyond over-familiarity.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: Nobody is why movies exist. Pure escapist perfection.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Nobody is pure escapism with preposterous situations, clearly defined and represented good guys and bad guys and a special effects team to bring it all to life.
reviews.author: Pamela Powell

reviews.text: (Bob) Odenkirk becomes the action movie star I never knew I needed.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: No one can play unassuming as credibly as Odenkirk.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: In a world filed with action films that take themselves too seriously, the cartoonishly violent Nobody wants to be like a court jester, by poking fun at the movie's characters and the action genre overall.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Weirdly entertaining in its mayhem with Bob Odenkirk, genius casting that leaves a mark, even in kick ass-ery. Who also kicks ass? Christopher "Doc Brown" Lloyd, that's who!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk comes on strong as an angry dad at war with the mob...the Better Call Saul star shows his street-fighter skills in violent but entertaining revenge film.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: This adrenaline-fueled thriller has style and attitude to spare, although the predictable nature of the mayhem blunts the cumulative impact.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Odenkirk deserves better. His conflicted character deserves better.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Nobody - a prime example of preposterous violence and brutal action tropes - feels derivative and self-conscious in its attempts to dish out as much cathartic vengeance as 91 minutes allows.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: I don't know if it's a good movie, but it's enjoyable, and I can certainly relate to the characters.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Few actors can balance a PTSD-riddled killer with the suburban dad aesthetic. Odenkirk excels at depicting duality, and the role of Hutch highlights his strengths
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: Luckily no animals were hurt in this paint-by-numbers JOHN WICK rip-off, but Odenkirk brings it as far as charisma and relatability. NOBODY doesn't reinvent the genre but you don't have to be a Keanu Reeves or Dwayne Johnson to play a tough guy.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: It feels unnecessary at best and irresponsible at worst.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: Fresh, enjoyable, and interesting.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: There's plenty here to love with numerous action set pieces, shocking moments of gore and violence, and even a bit of heart and emotion on a few occasions that elevate the film above your standard revenge thriller fare.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: An adult Home Alone meets John Wick.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: Nobody plays to Odenkirk's strengths and lets him shine in the role and kick some major ass in the process.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: It's entertaining, demented stuff, and you can see the filmmakers trying to kick off a franchise or a least a post-COVID sequel for when theatres are properly open at last.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: There's at least a few moments of more genuine inspiration, but there's nothing much more to see here, other than the empty calories of cartoonish violence.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: I will admit to being modestly disappointed by the whole endeavor.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: At 92 minutes, Nobody is a film that doesn't overstay its welcome and delivers big action and solid laughs. It's blunt. It's bloody. It's delicious.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Nobody is one giant, loud hyper-violent mess -- a John Wick wannabe that tries to pepper its action with dark humor but fails miserably.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Nobody is the Axe Body Spray of movies. It's pseudo cool, it leaves a lingering bad odor, and just because it'll find an appreciative audience of hormonal teenage boys doesn't mean it's actually any good.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: It's the wild, flying by the seat of your pants approach that makes Nobody work.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: Screenwriter Derek Kolstad helped elevate the entire genre with the John Wick series, and unfortunately, Nobody can't quite reach those heights. It still kicks a whole lot of ass, though.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: Odenkirk is perfectly cast as the title character, who is really less meek and more Jason Statham than folks might expect. The whole film may be an extended riff on this one joke, but it is a pretty funny joke.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: The undeniably talented director Ilya Naishuller keeps the action spry in Nobody but doesn't let us care about anyone or anything for too long.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: A much-needed shot of adrenaline in a slate of pandemic-year movies, a gripping, gleefully brutal, and yet emotionally affecting thriller.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Nobody moves along at an energetic pace, never wearing out its welcome by keeping to around 90 minutes in length and making the characters interesting, memorable and important...
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: Though it may not be reinventing the wheel, Nobody is a perfectly pulse-pounding blend of action and wit, made all the better by a charismatic performance from Odenkirk -- definitely proving that he does, in fact, have the chops to be a movie star.
reviews.author: Lauren Coates

reviews.text: A man does not expect to type the words "Bob Odenkirk, Badass Action Hero," yet the critic must admit that he is that man.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: A John Wick type film from the people who brought us and will being us more John Wick. Odenkirk is fun as always.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: A symphony of slapstick violence composed in brilliant clarity... The fracas reveals "Nobody" in its true form: a bleak action-comedy whose biggest laughs stem from a hunger for gratuitous brutality.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: A tug of war between how much you love Bob Odenkirk, and whether that's enough to disregard the movie's inferiority to Wick and Taken and the Equalizer films and all the rest.
reviews.author: Larry Carroll

reviews.text: Rocketing by at a lean hour and thirty minutes and packing a terrific soundtrack, tons of wickedly dry wit, and a tone that knows when to go over the top and when to pull back
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: Odenkirk nicely blends his past comedic and dramatic stylings into a highly satisfying and engaging hero character. (Full Content Review for Parents - Violence, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk aces his first role as an action star in this wild, twisty ride. He's such a canny, captivating actor that even when the plot gets silly you're willing to follow him anywhere.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Odenkirk is fantastic in the hard-hitting, action-packed role - you've never seen him like this before!
reviews.author: Kevin Brackett

reviews.text: The premise isn't new or unique but it's the kind of high-concept idea that, if done right, can be outrageously entertaining.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: The movie... seems designed to be chopped up into memes.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: Screenwriter Derek Kolstad creates the same man-against-the-world fury as he did writing the original "John Wick."
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Its staying power won't come from character depth or large-scale set-pieces, but its action beats should keep in heavy rotation with adrenaline junkies.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Action-packed from beginning to end, "Nobody" is a true cousin to films like "Death Wish" (the Bronson one, not the horrible Bruce Willis remake) and "Straw Dogs."
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Nobody whacked me square in the face. I wouldn't have wanted it any other way.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: By the end, one's senses are numb, even as the memory of certain amusing killings briefly flicker in the back of one's mind.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Nobody can't get over the fact that it cast Bob Odenkirk instead of letting the incredibly versatile actor tangle with the meaning of all this carnage. If only it took its own premise more seriously.
reviews.author: Chance Solem-Pfeifer

reviews.text: This is punishment as entertainment, a short and sour saga of a pacifist turned vengeful brute in order to win back his self-respect.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: "Nobody" is the "RED" of "John Wicks."
reviews.author: Neil Morris

reviews.text: Odenkirk makes for a surprisingly formidable action hero. And regardless of how derivative Nobody is of better films, hardcore action fans will find it hard to resist.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: In many ways, this feels like a "copy and paste" variant of a John Wick first draft... [But Bob Odenkirk] crushes it. He is so phenomenal in this movie.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: [Odenkirk's] presence and performance here elevate the material beyond what it might have been.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The film is not a bold refutation or reinvention of anything, but Nobody does - ironically enough - find some new life in its genre, mostly by honing it down to its most agile and clever.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: The result is not art - it doesn't want to be - but it is fun and that, as "Nobody" knows, is not nothing.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Nobody is not going to win any Oscars, unless they add in a stunt category sometime in the next year, but that doesn't make it any less entertaining.
reviews.author: Alex Bentley

reviews.text: A lot of fun, with great work from both Bob Odenkirk and director Ilya Naishuller. The third act falls apart, but still very much worth seeing.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Nobody certainly doesn't reinvent the wheel of its genre, but it beats it over the head enough with some skillful action and stylish direction from Naishuller.
reviews.author: Grant Hermanns

reviews.text: Odenkirk's presence at the center of this action-thriller makes it into an intriguing novelty. It could have been more, though.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Watching Odenkirk join the middle-aged action hero fold is pleasurable enough to make Nobody worth the while, even if it's an obvious echo of other, better recent films.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: Naishuller ultimately gets what matters here right, giving a talented actor an unexpected vehicle to drive really fast with just enough bloodshed for action fans, and not too much gore for average audiences.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: While essentially nothing more than a cartoonishly nasty graphic novel brought to life, 'Nobody' is...enjoyable if you can get past the basic absurdity.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: There's nothing new in this pointless, misguided mess. And violence as an aphrodisiac is not really what we wanted in 2021. Nobody comes out good in "Nobody."
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: Just like the best of the 1980s actioneers, Nobody has just the right mix of brains, brawn, and gut-busting laughs.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: It's a part we're so accustomed to [Odenkirk] playing that it makes the shift to legitimate action star utterly delightful, and the ease with which he shifts those gears is both unexpected and total perfection.
reviews.author: Vivian Kane

reviews.text: For anyone with a taste for the stylized violence and self-aware cartoonishness of the "John Wick" films - a taste for blood and mayhem that comes closer to corn syrup than most cinematic carnage - "Nobody" is a brutal treat.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: As slick as a blood spill and as single-minded as a meat grinder, "Nobody" hustles us along with a swiftness that blurs the foolishness of its plot and the depravity of its message.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: Nobody is a fine movie with inspired set pieces and enough delightful bits of violence and charm to make it an entertaining experience.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: The hyper-violent romp tries, and fails, to make us care about this reluctant hero.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: Arguably, "Nobody" is a man fighting for his dignity more than it is revenge film, but most of that is really just lost in a flurry of punches.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: The violence reaches Tarantino levels while the plot is as dangerously thin as a supermodel. But so what?
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: After so many other films in this subgenre, there's only so much mileage there, and the film's charm runs out fairly quickly.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: It's an exploration of self, a rumination on what's truly valuable in life, and that with family on your side you're strong enough, wrapped inside a darkly hilarious action thriller package.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Fun and fast-paced it may be the most unexpected good time at the movies since terrible people killed John Wick's dog.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A sturdy but familiar entry in the mindless shoot 'em up genre, Nobody hews so close to standards that it brings the whole genre into question.
reviews.author: Emily Wheeler

reviews.text: You can see [Bob Odenkirk's] sly winks to the audience present themselves every so often, selling this preposterous action flick that knows all too well how intelligent it needs to be in order to execute such a mindless idea.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk's performance, the hardcore action and the dry humor help trump the flaws on this satisfactory punch and shoot'em flick. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk is the action hero we never knew we needed in the adrenaline-driven Nobody, a thrill-filled John Wick for suburbia.
reviews.author: Rachel West

reviews.text: Despite the unoriginal premise, Nobody is a briskly directed action film that's worth a watch just for Odenkirk's performance.
reviews.author: Michelle Kisner

reviews.text: We can derive a lot of glee from watching Bob Odenkirk dismantle nameless goons, but what does that say about us?
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: The emotional beats don't land, and the plot threads are flimsy, but who cares? That's not why anyone is here.
reviews.author: Lindsay Traves

reviews.text: Ilya Naishuller's Nobody delivers the primal scream we need because it doesn't really hold back. More importantly, the central figure isn't a GQ cover boy... but a middle-aged man chained to a Costco shopping cart on weekends.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: "Nobody" ultimately turns out to be a simpler animal than that much-loved AMC series, and a lesser one.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Lamebrain dialogue, amateurish acting by much of the supporting cast and lazy character construction.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: 'Nobody' is a one-trick pony - in the form of a '72 Challenger and a barrage of aggression - but Odenkirk sells this ride.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: ...coming from a critic who did not like John Wick or John Wick 3 (John Wick 2 was admittedly pretty cool), I actually think that Nobody does it better.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Ninety-two fast-paced minutes of pure, bloody entertainment.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Nobody is a good action movie, while not a new premise, seeing Bob Odenkirk beat the tar out of people is very entertaining.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: "Nobody" goes exactly as expected, but it still carries an appealing revenge movie energy, and Odenkirk performs his superhero role with winning coarseness, helping to get the material to a place of unusual intimidation.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Beyond its utter hollowness, the most annoying thing about Nobody is the fact that it does have some good things in it that might have fared better with a stronger screenplay and better direction.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: I watched this with a giant grin on my face and even though it's early, Nobody is sure to go down as one of my favorite movies of 2021.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: If, like me, you found the assault of "Hardcore Henry" quickly became boringly repetitive despite a number of ingenious set-ups, but admire Odenkirk's work as Jimmy McGill, it won't be a surprise to learn that it is Odenkirk who carries this film
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It's all very been here, seen that yet there's something infinitely pleasing about a film doing very little but doing it very well, knowing just how high to aim without aiming any higher, aware of exactly what it can and can't do.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: While imperfect, Nobody is a damn sight better than the Bruce Willis Death Wish remake in capturing a normal man's vengeful rampage and inner conflict.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Simultaneously very grim and a helluva lot of fun, this sardonic revenge flick is the tale of a suburban dad who takes off his tame mask to reveal something much darker and bloodier.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Odenkirk's middle-aged melancholy and murderous glee is a winning combination throughout, providing enough spark between the slayings to make this the total suburban slaughter package.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: 'Nobody' is delightfully savage. It is too unbelievable to even try taking seriously. The film truly is a guilty-pleasure popcorn muncher.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Brimming with pointed dark humor and clever plot twists, "Nobody" revels in its B-Movie roots, Odenkirk providing a Charles Bronson-like turn that's surprising and entertaining as hell.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: Of course, what makes or breaks a film like this are the action scenes and they are plentiful and they are painful.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: Don't let the intentional slow start dissuade you, once the action kicks in, the pace ramps up and it's unrelenting, outrageous and highly entertaining.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The feel-good thrill ride of the summer arrives early. Move over John Wick, Hutch Mansell has arrived. Who?
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: Hollywood has a new action king, and it's Bob Odenkirk. Nobody is an action bonanza that will delight audiences.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Nobody is exactly what you expect it to be: a fun R-rated action thriller with brilliant bloody action and a riveting leading performance by Bob Odenkirk.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Don't be fooled by the initial concept or the title of the Better Call Saul/Breaking Bad actor's first starring macho, testosterone-loaded action flick, Odenkirk is the real deal without losing the persona for which we know him best.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: [Bob] Odenkirk's such an unlikely but likable action hero that hopefully Nobody is just the first installment of a new must-see action franchise.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: The Nordstrom Rack version of John Wick. The shared tailors don't traverse outside tradition. But this fits just fine. And there's a great surprise sewn into the sleeve with the pleasure of watching reed-thin Bob Odenkirk persuasively pummel people.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Odenkirk has ameliorate himself to audiences over the years as a non-threatening slime bag with a heart of gold but with Nobody, you'll believe that this 58-year old can tear limb from bust Chewbacca-style.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Relentlessly paced, brutally violent and packed with a charismatic lead star, IIya Naishuller's "Nobody" kicks unholy amounts of ass.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk's everyman quality makes him the most appealing action hero in ages. This movie is a blast.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: Like "The Foreigner" with Jackie Chan and Liam Neeson's "Taken" movies, "Nobody" belongs to relatively a new screen genre, in which it becomes very, very dangerous to make Dad angry.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: A rather chilly festival of carnage, too rigid to ever really spark to life. It's wickless.
reviews.author: Darren Franich

reviews.text: Odenkirk makes it work, elevating it to something beyond just a throwaway revenge movie with a paper-thin plot.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: While Nobody isn't a comedy per se, it has a few very funny moments, most of them courtesy of Hutch's father, David (Christopher Lloyd, Back to the Future Trilogy).
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: An action-packed & bloody blast from beginning to end!
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Yes, it's gruesome and violent, but it's also wickedly funny and surprisingly poignant. And while those Keanu comparisons are always going to be there, Nobody easily holds a candle to Wick.
reviews.author: Zaki Hasan

reviews.text: Nobody kicks all sorts of ass during its endlessly enjoyable runtime.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Impossible to find something bad to say about a movie this tailor made for me, personally.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: (Director) Naishuller delivers a virtuoso technical marvel of a movie with camera work, editing, sound design, and fight choreography that is mightily impressive. And yet, even with all that going for it, the movie simply feels way, way too familiar.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: No GoPro? No problem! Ilya Naishuller's latest proves he's a hugely promising action director in any format.
reviews.author: Perri Nemiroff

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk excels in the tough-guy role torn between restraining or indulging in violence. For the viewer, that choice is easier; celebrate the bloodbath that is Nobody
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: "Lean, mean and brutish, "Nobody" is best enjoyed as the juicy piece of pulp that it is. But Odenkirk, stepping into an action hero role for the first time, brings a sense of dolefulness and rue to this performance."
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: It's difficult not to enjoy the mayhem, especially when it's directed toward generic villains, but its excessiveness borders on the same tedium of Hutch's 9-to-5 job.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: If John Wick is Buster Keaton, [Odenkirk's] Hutch is Harold Lloyd.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: More violent lark than probing satire, but it's a wonderfully paced and consistently clever action movie that ups the ante of a genre that's been dominated by Liam Neeson clones.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: What starts out as interesting devolves into contrived and haphazard...
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: Naishuller's latest is a lean action-thriller full of visceral violence and biting humor. There's no depth in terms of narrative, but none of that matters much when this Odenkirk-led cast is having an absolute blast.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: 'Nobody' is a crowd-pleasing action endurance test that will be remembered for Bob Odenkirk's proven ability to bust skulls, intimidate thugs, and have an absolute blast getting as bloodied as possible.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: If you like the John Wick films, I suppose it's worth it.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Despite having just dispatched an entire warehouse full of criminals in gruesome fashion, Nobody wants to remind us that Hutch is still a decent guy, and I'll be damned if the innately charming Odenkirk doesn't make us believe it.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: Casting [Odenkirk] allows us to wrestle with preconceptions and enjoy the idea that you don't have to be as big as Daniel Bernhardt's "Bus Goon" to wreak havoc.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk is the best part of this disappointing John Wick clone.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Nobody offers more than enough gunplay and ass-kicking to satisfy grindhouse nuts. It also has plenty of pent-up rage and white male manslaughter to make others wince. In its purest form? Nobody is the premiere Dad Film of 2021.
reviews.author: Blake Goble

reviews.text: Nobody aces the thing it set out to do - it tells a character-driven story that turns Odenkirk into a bonafide action superstar. The fact they gave Doc Brown a cache of sawed-off shotguns is just the cherry on top of an excellent shootout sundae.
reviews.author: Adam Barnhardt

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk's self-proclaimed "Nobody" character packs enough heat and gritty bravado to make this high-octane action vehicle rev a lean, mean machine. Non-stop carnage and a total blast!
reviews.author: Preston Barta

reviews.text: I believe "nobody" can say that Odenkirk doesn't deserve to be on the middle-aged action stars list.
reviews.author: Jamie Broadnax

reviews.text: This is a gleefully violent action-comedy that strikes a masterful tone and consistently delivers thrills for its lean 92-minute running time.
reviews.author: Daniel Rutledge

reviews.text: Nobody doesn't just exist in the action genre but adds to it.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Nobody﻿ delivers plenty of hard-hitting action audiences expect, but the story lacks the emotional impact for the film to truly connect with viewers.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: Nothing radiates "I'm not a regular dad, I'm a cool dad" more than this film: so much style, little of anything else.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Nobody is an action-packed blast, and it proves that Bob Odenkirk can do anything.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: While waiting for [John Wick] Chapter 4, this makes for a rather satisfying entremets. [Full review in French]
reviews.author: Kevin N. Laforest

reviews.text: It's just hard to escape the feeling that the filmmakers sat down with a premise..."wouldn't it be funny if the Better Call Saul guy was John Wick?" and just never developed much of anything beyond that.
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: Odenkirk's presence does give the film a conflicted and darkly comic center. Let's hope more machine-gun antics are in his future.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Taking itself much less seriously than the Taken series and its predecessors, it's a wish-fulfillment romp just as ludicrous as any of them but more fun than most.
reviews.author: John DeFore

reviews.text: If ten years ago I had made a list of sentences I would never write in a review, surely "enjoying a Bob Odenkirk action movie" would have to have been one of them. And yet that reality has come to pass and mostly successfully.
reviews.author: Joshua Starnes

reviews.text: It's all insanely violent and gleefully silly.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: The film offers chaos by the yard with no real stakes or emotional reverberations.
reviews.author: Chuck Bowen

reviews.text: Is it a good movie? Not exactly. But its 90 minutes fly by, and it's a canny vehicle for Odenkirk, the unlikeliest star of a righteous macho bloodbath since Dustin Hoffman got his bear trap on in "Straw Dogs."
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: "Nobody" uses its boundaries as an asset. This giddy approach to action in place of story has held appeal ever since Wiley E. Coyote chased the Road Runner off a cliff, and "Nobody" lingers in a ludicrous plane that works in bite-sized pieces.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: Make no mistake, this is pure caveman bullshit. Yet it's caveman bullshit made with style and wit, qualities that extend from its screenplay to its performances to its staging.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk delightfully puts his 53-year-old self through stunt and fight coordinators to become a polo-shirted wraith of wanton violence.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: When the smoke has cleared and the broken bones are set, Nobody will stick with you as the kind of thrill ride a good action flick should be.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Bob Odenkirk was terrific here.
reviews.author: Dewey Singleton

synopsis: Emmy winner Bob Odenkirk (Better Call Saul, The Post, Nebraska) stars as Hutch Mansell, an underestimated and overlooked dad and husband, taking life's indignities on the chin and never pushing back. A nobody. When two thieves break into his suburban home one night, Hutch declines to defend himself or his family, hoping to prevent serious violence. His teenage son, Blake (Gage Munroe, The Shack), is disappointed in him and his wife, Becca (Connie Nielsen, Wonder Woman), seems to pull only further away. The aftermath of the incident strikes a match to Hutch's long-simmering rage, triggering dormant instincts and propelling him on a brutal path that will surface dark secrets and lethal skills. In a barrage of fists, gunfire and squealing tires, Hutch must save his family from a dangerous adversary (famed Russian actor Aleksey Serebryakov, Amazon's McMafia)--and ensure that he will never be underestimated as a nobody again.
